opti-1: Smoke rises over the Florida scrub.
opti-2: Fire sweeps through here every few years.
opti-3: A gopher tortoise heads down its burrow.
opti-4: The fire passes. The ground turns black.
opti-6: Two mice of the same kind. One is pale. One is darker.
opti-7: Could a small difference between two animals of the same kind change which one survives?
30-02-welcome: Our film starts on a fire day in the Florida scrub. First, inspect a mystery animal hiding in its shell.
30-02-lesson: Today you're a biologist. Follow a tortoise through a fire, run the Owl Test, then dig down Under the Burrow.
30-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
30-02-assign: Time to show what you learned. Name the science ideas, then draw two animals of the same kind with one variation.
how-30-02-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the animal, then tap three things you notice.
how-30-02-compare: Put the white sand under one tray and the dark soil under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Run the test. Then swap.
how-30-02-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing stop: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the photo shows.
how-30-02-det: Pick three cards, one at a time. Tap the variation you see, then name its animal group. Predict if the variation helps, hurts, or makes no real difference, and see the real place.
how-30-02-partc: Draw two individuals of the same Florida animal side by side. Show one variation between them, in a body part or a behavior. Label the variation on each one, and say which has the survival advantage.
